  "content": "# Ephemerides and in-situ solar wind for the 3I/ATLAS XMM-Newton epoch

Scope: `ephem/`, `insitu/`, `qc/{trajectories_hci_xy,timeseries_n_v_flux,coverage,crosscheck_preprint}.*`, `inventory.json`, `raw/{horizons,hapi,masters}/` and `scripts/`. Other folders in `data/` (adapt, boundary, cme, gong, hmi, ips, wsa_ccmc, scripts_rs, and the other files in `qc/`) belong to other tasks and are not described here.

XMM-Newton window: 2025-12-03T12:04:07 to 2025-12-04T10:11:54 UTC; midpoint 2025-12-03T23:08:00.5 UTC. Data span: 2025-10-01T00:00 to 2025-12-20T00:00 UTC.

## Rebuild

```
P=/home/scabot/miniconda3/bin/python3; Q=/home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python; cd scripts
$P fetch_horizons.py && $Q -I ephem.py
$P -I fetch_insitu.py && $P -I process_insitu.py && $P -I crosscheck.py && $P -I qc.py && $P -I inventory.py
```

Wrap heavy steps in `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=3G`. Downloads are cached; the scripts are idempotent. Peak memory is below 1 GB and each step runs in under 30 s once the cache is filled.

## Ephemerides (`ephem/<body>.csv`, hourly)

Bodies: 3i_atlas (Horizons `C/2025 N1`, solution JPL#54), earth 399, stereo_a -234, solar_orbiter -144, parker_solar_probe -96, bepicolombo -121, mars 499, maven -202, venus 299, mercury 199, juice -28, psyche -255, europa_clipper -159. ace -92 and wind -8 are included as extras.

Source: JPL Horizons API, `EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS`, `CENTER=500@10`, `REF_PLANE=FRAME` (ICRF), `VEC_CORR=NONE` (geometric, no light time), `TIME_TYPE=UT`, 1 h step. The raw text is in `raw/horizons/*_icrf.txt`.

Columns:
- `utc`: UTC time of the record.
- `x_hci_km, y_hci_km, z_hci_km` and `vx_hci, vy_hci, vz_hci` (km/s): Heliocentric Inertial, as in the sunpy `HeliocentricInertial` frame (Thompson 2006). Z is the IAU solar pole (RA 286.13 deg, Dec 63.87 deg). X is the ascending node of the solar equator on the mean J2000 ecliptic. HCRS to HCI is a constant rotation, taken from sunpy 8.0.1.
- `r_au`: heliocentric distance in AU (1 AU = 149597870.7 km).
- `hgi_lon_deg, hgi_lat_deg`: spherical HCI coordinates.
- `carr_lon_deg, carr_lat_deg`: sunpy `HeliographicCarrington` with `observer="earth"`. This applies the conventional Earth-observer light-time definition of the Carrington meridian, so all bodies share one rotating frame at each time. Using `observer="self"` instead would shift the comet by about 0.1 deg.
- `heeq_lon_deg, heeq_lat_deg`: sunpy `HeliographicStonyhurst`, with longitude wrapped to (-180, 180].
- `ecl_lon_deg, ecl_lat_deg`: heliocentric ecliptic J2000. This is the ICRF vector rotated by the IAU76 obliquity of 84381.448 arcsec, the convention of Horizons `refplane=ecliptic` that the preprint used.

Checks (`ephem/frame_checks.json`):
- HCI latitude agrees with Horizons `REF_PLANE=BODY` (IAU_SUN body equator) to 1e-14 deg at 9 epochs for the comet, Earth, STEREO-A and PSP. The longitude offset is a constant -61.1005 deg (peak-to-peak 1e-13 deg); it is the arc between the two nodes that define each frame's x-axis.
- Carrington longitude and latitude agree with the Horizons observer-table sub-observer point on the Sun (quantity 14, daily). The agreement is 3e-6 deg for Earth. For STEREO-A it is 0.003 deg, for Solar Orbiter 0.047 deg and for PSP 0.076 deg; these residuals equal the light-time difference between each spacecraft and Earth.
- Ecliptic longitude and radius reproduce the preprint tracks in `analysis_06_solar_wind/cache/track_*.tsv` to within 2e-6 deg and 5e-8 AU.

The comet geometry at the midpoint, cubic-interpolated from the hourly vectors, is in `ephem/comet_geometry_mid.json`:

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| r | 1.8734 AU |
| HGI lon / lat | 71.02 / -6.45 deg |
| Carrington lon / lat | 23.53 / -6.45 deg |
| HEEQ lon / lat | 75.06 / -6.45 deg |
| ecliptic lon / lat | 146.91 / 0.41 deg |
| HCI velocity | (60.60, 24.22, -7.01) km/s; magnitude 65.64 |
| radial / tangential | +43.13 / 49.48 km/s |
| tangential split | -49.43 in longitude (retrograde), +2.17 toward north |

Comet minus body longitude at the midpoint:

| body | HGI (deg) | ecliptic (deg) |
|---|---|---|
| Earth | +75.06 | +75.22 |
| STEREO-A | +24.95 | +24.84 |
| Solar Orbiter | +60.55 | +61.95 |
| PSP | +152.81 | +152.94 |
| Mars | -120.78 | -120.60 |

A positive value means the comet lies east of the body (prograde). Under pure corotation, a structure the body sees arrives at the comet's longitude Δλ/14.18 deg per day later; that is 1.76 d for STEREO-A and 5.29 d for Earth. Carrington and HEEQ separations equal the HGI separations.

## In-situ data (`insitu/`)

All in-situ data come from CDAWeb HAPI (`https://cdaweb.gsfc.nasa.gov/hapi`). Dataset IDs and parameter names were confirmed with `/catalog` and `/info`; the info files are in `raw/hapi/info/`. The raw HAPI CSV responses are stored gzipped, chunked by time, in `raw/hapi/<DATASET>/<start>_<end>_<paramhash>.csv.gz`. The CDAWeb master CDFs that define the flags are in `raw/masters/`.

Common processing:
- HAPI fill values and |x| >= 1e30 become NaN.
- Units: n in cm^-3, v in km/s, T in K (eV x 11604.518; thermal speed w gives T = m_p w^2 / 2k), B in nT.
- `utc` keeps each product's native time tag.
- Sub-minute products are reduced to 1-min means, labeled at the minute center (:30 s).

| file | dataset | parameters used | native tag | handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| omni_hro2_5min | OMNI_HRO2_5MIN | IMF, PLS, IMF_PTS, PLS_PTS, percent_interp, Timeshift, F, BX/BY/BZ_GSE, flow_speed, Vx/Vy/Vz (GSE), proton_density, T, NaNp_Ratio, Pressure | start of 5-min bin | shifted to the bow-shock nose; spacecraft ID columns kept |
| omni2_mrg1hr | OMNI2_H0_MRG1HR | IMF1800, PLS1800, *_PTS1800, ABS_B1800, F1800, BX/BY/BZ_GSE1800, T1800, N1800, V1800, PHI-V1800, THETA-V1800, Ratio1800, Pressure1800 | hour center (HH:30) | `B` = ABS_B, `B_vec` = F |
| stereo_a_pla_1dmax_1min | STA_L2_PLA_1DMAX_1MIN | error, attitude_flag, proton_number_density, proton_bulk_speed, proton_temperature, proton_thermal_speed, proton_n_s_flow_angle_inst | start of minute | validity cuts 0<n<500, 100<v<2000, 1e3<T<1e7 |
| stereo_a_magplasma_1min | STA_L2_MAGPLASMA_1M | BFIELDRTN, BTOTAL | start of minute | IMPACT/MAG |
| stereo_a_coho1hr | STA_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA | radialDistance, heliographicLat/Lon, BR/BT/BN, B, plasmaSpeed, plasmaDensity, plasmaTemp | start of hour | the dataset used by the preprint |
| solar_orbiter_pas_grnd_mom_1min | SOLO_L2_SWA-PAS-GRND-MOM | quality_factor, N, V_RTN, T | sample center, 1 s (4 s in places) | 1-min means; a sample is rejected if any of N, V_RTN or T is missing; `quality_factor` is the minute mean |
| solar_orbiter_mag_rtn_1min | SOLO_L2_MAG-RTN-NORMAL-1-MINUTE | B_RTN | minute center | |
| solar_orbiter_coho1hr | SOLO_COHO1HR_MERGED_MAG_PLASMA | as STA, plus VR/VT/VN, ProtonSpeed, protonDensity, protonTemp | start of hour | the dataset used by the preprint |
| parker_solar_probe_spi_sf00_l3_mom_1min | PSP_SWP_SPI_SF00_L3_MOM | QUALITY_FLAG, DENS, VEL_RTN_SUN, TEMP, SUN_DIST | sample center | samples with QUALITY_FLAG bits 0, 2, 3, 8, 10 or 11 are rejected; DENS >= 0.01 required; 1-min means |
| parker_solar_probe_mag_rtn_1min | PSP_FLD_L2_MAG_RTN_1MIN | psp_fld_l2_mag_RTN_1min | minute center | |
| ace_swe_k1 | AC_K1_SWE | Np, Vp, He_ratio, Tpr | hour center (CDF: "Time, centered") | preliminary browse data; `He_ratio` is stored as a fraction, despite its "%" unit label |
| ace_mfi_h1 | AC_H1_MFI | Magnitude, BGSEc | 4 min | |
| wind_swe_h1 | WI_H1_SWE | fit_flag, Proton_V/VX/VY/VZ_nonlin, Proton_W_nonlin, Proton_Np_nonlin, Alpha_Na_nonlin, BX/BY/BZ | start of spectrum, about 92 s | proton parameters set to NaN when fit_flag < 2 (0 = no fit, 1 = poor peak identification) |
| maven_insitu_kp_upstream_1min | MVN_INSITU_KP-4SEC | SWIA_Hplus_density (+DQ), SWIA_Hplus_flow_velocity_MSO (+DQ), SWIA_Hplus_temperature (+DQ), MAG_field_MSO, SPICE_spacecraft_MSO | 4 s | upstream selection below; 1-min means; only upstream minutes are written |

`hourly_<mission>.csv` (omni, wind, ace, stereo_a, solar_orbiter, parker_solar_probe, maven) has columns `utc,n,v,T,B,vr`, plus `na_np` (alpha/proton density ratio) for omni, wind and ace.
- Grid: bins [HH:00, HH+1:00), labeled at the bin center HH:30. The grid is complete from 2025-10-01T00:30 to 2025-12-19T23:30, so missing hours appear as NaN rows.
- Mean: a column's value is the mean of its valid samples. It is kept only when the summed sample durations cover at least 50% of the bin. A sample's duration is the smaller of its two neighbor spacings, capped at the bin width. For 1-min means, the duration is the covered fraction of the minute.
- ACE K1: these hours are center-tagged, so each K1 value enters as two half-hour samples. Each output bin is then the time-weighted mean of the two K1 hours it overlaps.
- Sources:
  - omni: OMNI_HRO2_5MIN.
  - wind: WI_H1_SWE; B is |(BX,BY,BZ)| from that file.
  - ace: K1 SWE plus H1 MFI.
  - stereo_a: PLASTIC 1-min plus IMPACT 1-min.
  - solar_orbiter: PAS 1-min plus MAG 1-min.
  - parker_solar_probe: SPAN-I 1-min plus FIELDS 1-min. Plasma is masked where SUN_DIST > 0.3 AU.
  - maven: KP upstream 1-min.
- `vr`:
  - OMNI and Wind: -Vx(GSE).
  - SolO: V_R (RTN).
  - PSP: VEL_RTN_SUN R.
  - MAVEN: -Vx(MSO).
  - STEREO-A and ACE: NaN, because no vector velocity is available (use `v`).

## Cross-check against the preprint caches (`qc/crosscheck_preprint.json`, `qc/crosscheck_preprint.png`)

The preprint caches cover 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-29; the overlap with this work is 2025-11-08 to 2025-12-19. Before comparing, the cache values are given the preprint's own validity filter (0.01<n<500, 100<v<1500, PLS1800 = 52).
- Same products:
  - SolO COHO, ACE K1 and OMNI2 are identical to the caches (max |Δ| = 0).
  - STA COHO differs by at most 0.05 cm^-3 and 0.5 km/s, a rounding-level difference that suggests a reprocessing since the cache was made.
- Hourly means rebuilt from high-resolution data:
  - Binned on [tag, tag+1 h), STA PLASTIC 1-min reproduces STA COHO with median ratio 1.000, |Δn| <= 0.005, |Δv| <= 0.05.
  - SolO PAS reproduces SolO COHO with median ratio 1.000; all hours agree within 1% in n and 0.3% in v.
  - Binning on [tag-30 min, tag+30 min) is clearly worse: only 65% of STA hours agree within 10%. This confirms that COHO tags mark the start of the hour, as the CDF states.
- OMNI: hourly means of OMNI_HRO2 against the cached OMNI2 give median ratio 1.000 and r(log n) = 0.988.
- Wind: unshifted Wind H1 matches cached OMNI2 best at a +1 h lag (median n ratio 1.004, r(log n) = 0.995). This lag is the propagation shift from Wind to the bow-shock nose.
- ACE K1 against Wind H1 for the same hour: v ratio 0.996, but the median n ratio is 0.66, with 5–95% range 0.20–0.96. The preprint scaled ACE n by a fixed factor of 1.7, which corresponds to a ratio of 0.59.
- Preprint timing: the preprint used COHO start-of-hour tags as sample times, while its OMNI2 tags are hour centers. This mixes conventions with a 30-min offset; the effect is small compared with the mapping uncertainty.

## Caveats and decisions

- No contemporaneous heavy-ion composition exists on CDAWeb for October–December 2025:
  - ACE SWICS (AC_H3_SW2) ends 2025-03-16. The ACE Science Center SWICS 2.0 file for 2025 also stops at DOY 76.
  - AC_H6_SWI ends 2024-12-31.
  - Solar Orbiter SWA-HIS L3 (SOLO_L3_SWA-HIS-COMP-10MIN) ends 2023-04-27, and ESA SOAR also has no HIS science products after 2023-04-28.
  - STA PLASTIC Fe charge states end in 2011.
  - The only composition columns are therefore alpha/proton ratios (OMNI NaNp_Ratio, Wind Na/Np, ACE K1 He_ratio).
- ACE SWEPAM:
  - Level 2 (AC_H0_SWE) ends 2024-07-09, both on CDAWeb and at the ASC, so only the preliminary K1 browse data exist for this period.
  - K1 densities run low against Wind (median ratio 0.66) and show deep dropouts around Nov 14–20. Use ACE for speed and structure, not for absolute n.
- OMNI: for the whole period both OMNI_HRO2 IMF and PLS are 100% Wind (ID 52), and OMNI2 uses IDs 51/52. OMNI therefore adds no independent spacecraft; it is Wind time-shifted to the bow-shock nose.
- DSCOVR: DSCOVR_H1_FC on CDAWeb ends 2019-06-27, and the NCEI DSCOVR archive has moved behind a portal, so DSCOVR was not used.
- Wind: WI_K0_SWE was also fetched (`raw/hapi/WI_K0_SWE`) but rejected, because QF_V and QF_Np are never 0 in this period and their semantics could not be confirmed. Wind H1 has many gaps; OMNI is the more complete L1 series.
- STEREO-A PLASTIC:
  - The 2025 L2 files carry no RTN velocity, no E/W flow angle (fill) and no `caution` flag. Requesting any of those parameters makes HAPI return "no data", so they were dropped.
  - The `error` and `attitude_flag` columns are empty but kept.
  - COHO flow angles are fill.
- Solar Orbiter PAS:
  - `quality_factor` has no definition in the CDF metadata or the PAS user guide. It is kept as a column and not used for filtering; COHO does not filter on it either.
  - Hours where V_RTN is missing but N exists (for example 2025-12-05T15 to 12-06T13, with T near 5e5 K) are rejected entirely, which matches COHO.
- Parker Solar Probe:
  - SPC L3I returns no data from October to December 2025.
  - SPAN-I partial moments outside encounter (SUN_DIST 0.4–0.73 AU, before 2025-12-06) give n of about 0.1–2 cm^-3, roughly 10x below expectation, because of the field-of-view and heat-shield blockage of the partial moments. They are kept in the 1-min file, with `sun_dist_au`, but masked in the hourly file.
  - Encounter 26 perihelion is 2025-12-13T07 UT at 0.0459 AU. Partial-moment densities may still be biased low.
- MAVEN:
  - KP-4SEC is used instead of ONBOARDSVYMOM because KP carries MSO positions.
  - Upstream samples must satisfy all of the following:
    - position outside 1.2x the Vignes et al. (2000) bow shock (X0 = 0.64 RM, ε = 1.03, L = 2.04 RM, RM = 3389.5 km);
    - SWIA density DQ = 1;
    - |v| > 200 km/s and -Vx(MSO) > 0;
    - T < 1e6 K.
  - Beyond 1.2x the median B levels off at about 3.8 nT. Samples above 1e6 K show upstream-like B and are treated as onboard-moment artifacts.
  - Onboard moments assume 100% protons, so T is biased high (median about 2e5 K).
  - A density excursion to 50–125 cm^-3 on 2025-10-29, with B about 11 nT, is retained as possibly real.
  - Mars solar conjunction is in January 2026, and CDAWeb data stop on 2025-12-05.
- BepiColombo is 21 deg and Mercury 7 deg in HGI longitude from the comet at about 0.35 AU, but no BepiColombo cruise plasma or field data are on CDAWeb.
- HAPI sometimes returns a record outside the requested interval, for example at the edge of a gap. Each chunk is clipped to its own [start, end) range.
